## What this is

Four pieces of open-source work I did with Claude Code, why I reach for it
rather than Positron, and how it is set up.

Everything shown here is public. None of it touches clinical data.

::: {.notes}
Set the boundary in the first minute. It is the question the room is holding.
:::

# What it built

## 1. A bug fix in xgxr, through to CRAN

- Fixed the scale-transform break (issue #72)
- Found and removed a hyperlink whose TLS certificate had expired, which is
  the kind of thing CRAN rejects a submission for
- Updated `cran-comments.md`, ran win-builder, recorded the result
- Now at version 1.1.6

The tedious half of a CRAN release is checks, comments and re-checks. That
half is what got absorbed.

## 2. xgx onto modern CI

- The rendered HTML used to live in the repository
- Now `build-site.yml` builds it, so the site is a build product rather than a
  committed artifact
- Added the data-checking page

::: {.notes}
The point: it did the CI plumbing, which is the part nobody in the group wants
to spend a weekend on.
:::

## 3. A new package: synpmx

**Structurally Faithful Synthetic Pharmacometric Data**

Generating realistic synthetic PK/PD datasets, so workflows, teaching material
and tooling can be developed and shared without exposing real clinical data.

Written from nothing to a working package with a pkgdown site.

## 4. A strategic question, not a coding task

**Does intra-patient dose escalation reach a confirmable active dose sooner in
a first-in-human T-cell engager trial?**

What came back was not code. It was a specification, a reading queue, and a
references page marking, for every source, whether the claim drawn from it had
actually been checked against the source.

::: {.notes}
This is the one that surprised me. Worth dwelling on.
:::

# How it is set up

## The pattern: it builds a website, and I read the website

::: {.incremental}
- It works, commits, and pushes
- CI publishes the site
- I look at the rendered output — on my phone, at home, or at work
- No local environment, no screen sharing, no "can you paste the output"
:::

**And it sets all of that up itself.** The Actions workflow, the publishing,
the theme.

::: {.notes}
This is the transferable idea. Everything else is detail.
:::

## Why Claude Code rather than Positron

::: {.incremental}
1. **It runs longer with less input.** Fewer round trips per unit of work.
2. **It runs on my own machine at home, against ordinary GitHub.** No
   confusion with the Copilot setup.
3. **I can drive it from my phone, my home machine, or my work machine**
   with remote control.
4. **I can choose the model.** Though I was moved from Fable to Opus once the
   work touched biology.
:::

## What I actually do

One command from my home machine:

```
/remote-control
```

And often not even that. A fresh session checks the repository out and picks
up where the last one stopped, because the state lives in the repository
rather than in the session.

# The parts that need care

## What I check, every time

The model produces plausible output. Plausible is not the same as correct, and
the reviewer is still the author.

- Does the code run, and do the tests pass?
- Is every number traceable to something I can open?
- For a claim from a paper, has it been checked against the paper?

The TCE-IPDE references page carries a status marker on every source for
exactly this reason.

::: {.notes}
Ties to the "AI can assist, humans must own decisions" position. Do not skip
this slide — it is what makes the rest credible to this room.
:::

## If you want to try it

1. Do the training, so `claude.ai` is not blocked
2. Pick a repository with **no** sensitive data
3. Give it a small, checkable task — a failing test, a CI workflow
4. Have it publish a site, so you can read the output rather than run it
5. Write a `CLAUDE.md` for the repository once the conventions matter
